newsitem.title: CHINA: IPO market seen picking up in Hong Kong's new era.
newsitem.headline: IPO market seen picking up in Hong Kong's new era.

text.p: Activity in Hong Kong's initial public offering (IPO) market is seen picking after the territory's reversion to China last week, corporate finance executives said on Monday.
The IPO market was quiet in the past few weeks as investors mostly stayed on the sidelines and many merchant bankers were not in the market during the handover holidays, they said.

"Earlier in May and June, the market had already expected there would not be much activity during the handover period and that was why not much happened during the period," said Eugene Law, director at Lippo Securities.
"It is a kind of self fulfilling prophecy," Law said.
Analysts said people adopting a wait-and-see attitude due to uncertainty about how the market would be after the handover also led to a quieter IPO market in the beginning of new era in Hong Kong.

"Many people would prefer not to do anything during the period because no one knew what would happen in the market and were unsure whether there would be any drastic movements during the period," Law added.

Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule at midnight of June 30. As the handover went smoothly and appeared to be positively received worldwide, activity in the IPO market was expected to pick up later in July, analysts said.
"I did not see any negative impact or loss in confidence after the handover, confidence remains strong," said Patrick Cheng, corporate finance director of HSBC Investment Banking.

"Sentiment is very positive in the long run because the transition has run very smoothly," Cheng said. "As many people were on holiday during the handover, activity (in the IPO market) is seen picking up following the holiday."
"The market liquidity is still high and that can give strong support to the IPOs," Law said.
Analysts said they expected several new listings would kick off their IPOs later in July.

Property firm Winsan (China) Investment, which was expected to issue 250 million shares at HK$2.01 per share, has held a presentation for analysts on Monday. Dealing in shares is expected to begin in July 24.

Angang New Steel Co Ltd is expected to issue 890 million H-shares at price ranging from HK$1.61 to HK$1.97 per share. A presentation for analysts is expected on Wednesday. H-shares are shares in China incorporated enterprises listed in Hong Kong.
China Southern Airlines is expected to seek a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York later this month or in early August.
"As no new IPOs were being launched during the last couple of days (after the handover), many people were still staying on the sideline to see how the market like," Cheng said.

"Underlying fundamentals are not bad, there is a lot of liquidity in the market waiting for right idea," Law said. "The wave of IPO demand will return if the first few issues (after the handover) perform nicely."
But analysts said investors would take a more selective approach on IPOs on expectation that more new listings would come onto the market in the next six months.
"People are tending to be more selective, the focus will be on good quality stocks which have their market niche and strong management," said Joseph Law, director of Jardine Fleming.

Despite underlying strong market sentiment in the long run, analysts said concern about the magnitude of the impact from possible government measures to curb property speculation might dampen the market strength in the near term.
"Many will stay on the sidelines to see what the impact will be," Cheng said. "The sooner the measures are clarified and the uncertainty is removed, the more the market will benefit."
Law said: "we remain optimistic over the long term sentiment of the (IPO) market."
